module: Define the release and assessment boundary

lesson.title: Case: record the release boundary
lesson.summary: Record the boundary of two fictional releases.

prerequisites.reason: A release scope conclusion cannot ignore a prohibition.
The dated case must distinguish a new release from an existing-system transition.
The medical case needs the procedure priority when routes overlap.
The case needs a defined evidence dossier before it can record unresolved release gaps.

blocks: **Case facts:** Northbridge v1 materially ranks recruitment applicants for a private employer. Harbour v1 analyses diagnostic images; this exercise stipulates an Annex I Section A medical product with a sector-required third party. Both providers ask whether their releases are ready. No real customer or device is being classified.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 3, 5, 6, 43(3), 111(2), 113; Annex IV

blocks: Start with intended purpose, version, named provider and release countries/date. Check prohibited practices independently. Northbridge's stipulated Annex III employment use supports its high-risk route. Harbour's stipulated sector facts support the relevant product-law route; its actual device class is outside this exercise.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 3, 5, 6, 43(3), 111(2), 113; Annex IV

blocks: The proposed Northbridge release is during an unresolved transitional period. Record the Section 5/Sections 1–3 interaction and refer it for dated interpretation. Harbour's body has not supplied the transitional competence evidence. Record that as an assessor evidence gap, not as an automatically valid appointment.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Articles 3, 5, 6, 43(3), 111(2), 113; Annex IV

blocks: The **scope record** should distinguish a supported conclusion, an explicit case assumption and an unknown needing evidence. Add the technical-file gaps from F05. A readiness verdict must be limited to the questions actually checked; it is not a comprehensive legal clearance.
